requirement:
An outline input MUST be rewritten only if the mapped node exists and its
structural hash, computed under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash` over the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` text of the node, equals the recorded
hash.
rationale:
`requirements.refactor.outline_inputs` has three testable obligations. An outline input is rewritten only if (a) the mapped node exists and (b) its structural hash, computed over the mapped-back text, equals the recorded hash. The reviewed tests cover each of these, both when the input is rewritten and when it is not.

- **Rewrite when the node exists and the hash matches.**
  - `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_function_keeps_its_evidence_current]` moves `fn[load]` to `src/config/load.rs`. It asserts that `evidence/rules.load.json` is changed and that `inputs[1].file` becomes `src/config/load.rs`. It also asserts that `errors(root)` is empty afterwards, so the rewritten hash is current. It checks that an unaffected record is left byte-identical, and that a second run changes 0 records.
  - The same test shows an input that reads no moved node is left alone.
- **Mapped node missing, so no rewrite.** `tests/refactor.rs#fn[an_input_whose_node_is_missing_after_the_move_is_not_rewritten]` moves the file but leaves `fn[verify]` behind. It asserts the report says `no outline node matches "fn[verify]"`. It also asserts the record file is byte-identical to its earlier contents.
- **Node exists but its hash differs, so no rewrite.** `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_function_edited_while_moving_leaves_its_records_stale]` adds a statement to the function while moving it. It asserts the report line `inputs[1]: src/config/load.rs#fn[load] no longer has the recorded hash`. It asserts the record is unchanged and that `errors(root)` stays non-empty.
- **Hash computed over the mapped-back text.**
  - `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_rename_rewrites_the_hash_of_a_node_whose_doc_comment_names_it]` renames `rules.load` to `core.load`. A doc comment, which is hashed, names the requirement, so the current text differs from the recorded text.
  - The test asserts the new hash differs from the old one (`assert_ne!`). It then asserts the record's `inputs[1].hash` equals the new hash.
  - This passes only if the comparison against the recorded hash is made on the mapped-back text. Otherwise the hash would mismatch and the input would not be rewritten.
- **The mapped-back transformation itself.** `src/refactor/tests.rs#fn[mapped_back_text_replaces_whole_new_names_and_paths]` tests `text_back`. It covers whole-name and whole-path replacement, longer names and look-alike paths left alone, and node addresses mapped back.

The structural hash rule is cited as context, so I did not reassess its own tests. The tests cover both the rewrite and the non-rewrite outcomes, with assertions on the report text and on the record contents. I found no adequacy gap.

text: :::{req} outline_inputs
An outline input MUST be rewritten only if the mapped node exists and its
structural hash, computed under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash` over the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` text of the node, equals the recorded
hash.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{definition} mapped_back
:phrase: mapped-back
The *mapped-back* form of current text or a current address is the text or
address with each new side of the mappings replaced by its old side.
